rows.description: A student trusts his gut in a field he barely knows and is often wrong. Reliable intuition comes only from many repeated experiences with quick, honest feedback.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26

rows.description: A young nurse, engineer or driver begins to sense that something is wrong before she can say why, from hundreds of cases seen. She learns to treat the feeling as a cue to check.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22

rows.description: A senior notices experts confident in fields with noisy feedback, such as predicting markets or hiring, where experience does not sharpen judgment. He asks for data alongside gut feeling.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22

rows.description: A mature professional trusts a trained hunch in familiar settings, tests it against evidence, checks with colleagues, and stays humble outside her domain.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22

rows.description: A toddler believes that his wish or a gesture can make things happen, such as a wave making a toy move. He cannot yet separate thought from the physical world.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17

rows.description: A preschooler believes in monsters under the bed, the tooth fairy and special words that protect him. Imagination is vivid and the line with reality is soft.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17

rows.description: A young child thinks his angry wish caused a sibling's illness or parents' quarrel. Adults should gently explain that his thoughts did not cause it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17

rows.description: A parent plays along with imagination, checks the child's fears, and gently gives simple true explanations, without mocking him or scaring him with made-up dangers.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17
related mind states: affection, anger, fear

rows.description: An older child avoids stepping on cracks, taps things or wears a lucky shirt for exams. He half knows it is not logical and still feels safer with it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17

rows.description: A teacher notices teenagers who still keep lucky charms or fear jinxing good news. It is normal and harmless when it does not replace effort or lead to harmful choices.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12
